claim: In plants, algae and cyanobacteria, Photosystem II (PSII) catalyzes the light-driven splitting of water at a protein-bound Mn4CaO5-cluster, the water-oxidizing complex (WOC).
source: In plants, algae and cyanobacteria, Photosystem II (PSII) catalyzes the light-driven splitting of water at a protein-bound Mn4CaO5-cluster, the water-oxidizing complex (WOC).
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about PSII function in oxygenic photosynthesis.

claim: The light-driven formation of the WOC from dissolved metal ions is essential in both initial activation and continuous repair of PSII.
source: In the photosynthetic organisms, the light-driven formation of the WOC from dissolved metal ions is a key process because it is essential in both initial activation and continuous repair of PSII.
evidence: This statement is presented as established knowledge about PSII assembly and repair.

claim: A structure of PSII from Thermosynechococcus elongatus without the Mn4CaO5-cluster was obtained for the first time.
source: For the first time, we obtained a structure of PSII from Thermosynechococcus elongatus without the Mn4CaO5-cluster.
evidence: This is a primary finding reported by the authors based on their crystallographic data.

claim: Cluster-removal leaves the positions of all coordinating amino acid residues and most nearby water molecules largely unaffected.
source: Surprisingly, cluster-removal leaves the positions of all coordinating amino acid residues and most nearby water molecules largely unaffected, resulting in a pre-organized ligand shell for kinetically competent and error-free photo-assembly of the Mn4CaO5-cluster.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the apo-PSII crystal structure data.

claim: The pre-organized ligand shell results in kinetically competent and error-free photo-assembly of the Mn4CaO5-cluster.
source: Surprisingly, cluster-removal leaves the positions of all coordinating amino acid residues and most nearby water molecules largely unaffected, resulting in a pre-organized ligand shell for kinetically competent and error-free photo-assembly of the Mn4CaO5-cluster.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the structural data regarding the functional implications of the pre-organized ligand shell.

claim: A specific bi-manganese cluster, likely a di-µ-oxo bridged pair of Mn(III) ions, is an assembly intermediate.
source: First experiments initiating (i) partial disassembly and (ii) partial re-assembly after complete depletion of the Mn4CaO5-cluster agree with a specific bi-manganese cluster, likely a di-µ-oxo bridged pair of Mn(III) ions, as an assembly intermediate.
evidence: This is based on partial assembly/disassembly crystallographic data and comparison with previous XAS studies.

claim: The Mn4CaO5-cluster catalyzes the oxidation of two molecules of water yielding molecular oxygen, four protons and four 'energized' electrons.
source: In the last decade, X-ray crystal structures of the dimeric PSII core complexes (dPSIIcc) from the thermophilic cyanobacteria Thermosynechococcus elongatus (T. elongatus) (Zouni et al., 2001; Ferreira et al., 2004; Loll et al., 2005; Guskov et al., 2009; Hellmich et al., 2014) and Thermosynechococcus vulcanus (T. vulcanus) (Umena et al., 2011; Suga et al., 2015) showed that each monomer contains at least 20 protein subunits including nearly 100 cofactors and an inorganic metal-cluster, designated as the Mn4CaO5-cluster, which catalyzes the oxidation of two molecules of water yielding molecular oxygen, four protons and four 'energized' electrons (McEvoy and Brudvig, 2006; Barber, 2009; Dau et al., 2012; Cox and Messinger, 2013; Yano and Yachandra, 2014; Shen, 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the catalytic function of the Mn4CaO5-cluster, supported by citations.

claim: Each PSII monomer contains at least 20 protein subunits including nearly 100 cofactors.
source: In the last decade, X-ray crystal structures of the dimeric PSII core complexes (dPSIIcc) from the thermophilic cyanobacteria Thermosynechococcus elongatus (T. elongatus) (Zouni et al., 2001; Ferreira et al., 2004; Loll et al., 2005; Guskov et al., 2009; Hellmich et al., 2014) and Thermosynechococcus vulcanus (T. vulcanus) (Umena et al., 2011; Suga et al., 2015) showed that each monomer contains at least 20 protein subunits including nearly 100 cofactors and an inorganic metal-cluster, designated as the Mn4CaO5-cluster, which catalyzes the oxidation of two molecules of water yielding molecular oxygen, four protons and four 'energized' electrons (McEvoy and Brudvig, 2006; Barber, 2009; Dau et al., 2012; Cox and Messinger, 2013; Yano and Yachandra, 2014; Shen, 2015).
evidence: This is based on previous crystal structures of PSII from T. elongatus and T. vulcanus.

claim: In cyanobacteria, three membrane-extrinsic subunits are located at the lumenal side of the thylakoid membrane: PsbO (33 kDa), PsbV (cyt c-550) and PsbU (12 kDa).
source: In cyanobacteria, three membrane-extrinsic subunits are located at the lumenal side of the thylakoid membrane: PsbO (33 kDa), PsbV (cyt c-550) and PsbU (12 kDa) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is established structural knowledge about cyanobacterial PSII, supported by citations and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The extrinsic subunits PsbO, PsbV, and PsbU interact with intrinsic membrane proteins and stabilize the Mn4CaO5-cluster.
source: They interact with intrinsic membrane proteins and stabilize the Mn4CaO5-cluster (Bricker et al., 2012; Nickelsen and Rengstl, 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the function of extrinsic subunits, supported by citations.

claim: The atomic-resolution structure at 1.9 Å of dPSIIcc from T. vulcanus enables a detailed geometry of the Mn4CaO5-cluster.
source: At present, the atomic-resolution structure at 1.9 Å of dPSIIcc from T. vulcanus enables a detailed geometry of the Mn4CaO5-cluster (Umena et al., 2011; Tanaka et al., 2017).
evidence: This refers to the high-resolution structure from Umena et al., 2011.

claim: The shape of the Mn4CaO5-cluster was described as a 'distorted chair': A Mn3CaO4 heterocubane cluster ('chair base') with an additional Mn (Mn4) in exo position connected to the cubane by two µ-oxo-bridges ('backrest').
source: The shape of the Mn4CaO5-cluster was described as a 'distorted chair': A Mn3CaO4 heterocubane cluster ('chair base') with an additional Mn (Mn4) in exo position connected to the cubane by two µ-oxo-bridges ('backrest') (Umena et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a description from the high-resolution structure by Umena et al., 2011.

claim: Four water molecules are directly ligated to the Mn4CaO5-cluster, two (W1, W2) at Mn4 and the other two (W3, W4) at Ca2+.
source: Further, four water molecules are directly ligated to the Mn4CaO5-cluster, two (W1, W2) at Mn4 and the other two (W3, W4) at Ca2+.
evidence: This is structural information from the high-resolution PSII structure.

claim: The whole cluster is coordinated by six amino acids from the D1 subunit (PsbA) and one from the CP43 protein (PsbC).
source: The whole cluster is coordinated by six amino acids from the D1 subunit (PsbA) and one from the CP43 protein (PsbC).
evidence: This is structural information from the high-resolution PSII structure.

claim: The incubation of dPSIIcc with NH2OH/EDTA in solution caused the loss of all the three extrinsic subunits (PsbU, PsbV and PsbO).
source: Interestingly, the incubation of dPSIIcc with NH2OH/EDTA in solution not only caused the loss of all the three extrinsic subunits (PsbU, PsbV and PsbO), but also a dissociation of dimeric into monomeric PSIIcc.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from SDS-PAGE and gel filtration experiments.

claim: The incubation of dPSIIcc with NH2OH/EDTA in solution caused a dissociation of dimeric into monomeric PSIIcc.
source: Interestingly, the incubation of dPSIIcc with NH2OH/EDTA in solution not only caused the loss of all the three extrinsic subunits (PsbU, PsbV and PsbO), but also a dissociation of dimeric into monomeric PSIIcc.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from gel filtration and BN-PAGE experiments.

claim: All 20 protein subunits and cofactors remained largely unaffected in the absence of the metal-cluster.
source: Surprisingly, we found that all 20 protein subunits and cofactors remained largely unaffected in the absence of the metal-cluster.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the apo-PSII crystal structure.

claim: Small changes in apo-PSIIcc are limited to residues in the vicinity of the cluster and a destabilization of the PsbU subunit.
source: Small changes in apo-PSIIcc are limited to residues in the vicinity of the cluster and a destabilization of the PsbU subunit.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the apo-PSII crystal structure and B-factor analysis.

claim: Treatment of dPSIIcc solutions with NH2OH caused loss of O2 evolution activity.
source: When we treated dPSIIcc solutions with NH2OH, they lost O2 evolution activity (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from oxygen evolution measurements.

claim: In the dark-stable S1-state of PSII, the WOC is a high valent Mn complex (MnIII2 MnIV2).
source: In the dark-stable S1-state of PSII, the WOC is a high valent Mn complex (MnIII2 MnIV2).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the oxidation states of Mn in the S1 state.

claim: The addition of NH2OH reduces the Mn ions to Mn2+, which is no longer stably bound to the PSII apo-protein.
source: The addition of NH2OH reduces the Mn ions to Mn2+, which is no longer stably bound to the PSII apo-protein.
evidence: This is an inference based on the known reducing properties of NH2OH and the loss of Mn from PSII.

claim: A combination of NH2OH and EDTA in dPSIIcc solutions caused dissociation of all three extrinsic subunits, PsbU, PsbV and PsbO, whereas all other protein subunits remained bound to PSII.
source: A combination of NH2OH and EDTA in dPSIIcc solutions caused dissociation of all three extrinsic subunits, PsbU, PsbV and PsbO, whereas all other protein subunits remained bound to PSII (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A for larger PSII subunits; Supplementary file 2 for smaller PSII subunits).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from SDS-PAGE analysis.

claim: The absence of PsbO could destabilize the monomer-monomer interaction in the PSII core dimer.
source: In addition, the absence of PsbO could destabilize the monomer-monomer interaction in the PSII core dimer (Boekema et al., 2000; Komenda et al., 2010), leading to a monomerization (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is based on previous studies and observed monomerization in gel filtration experiments.

claim: Treatment of dPSIIcc solution only with EDTA at 50 mM removed only the PsbU subunit.
source: To further understand the disassembly process, we also treated the dPSIIcc solution only with EDTA at 50 mM. Under this condition, only the PsbU subunit was removed.
evidence: This is an experimental observation from protein analysis.

claim: PsbU is comparatively loosely bound in the PSIIcc.
source: This result indicates that PsbU is comparatively loosely bound in the PSIIcc.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that EDTA alone removes PsbU.

claim: >30 mM NH2OH are needed in C12E8 dPSIIcc microcrystals to reduce all the Mn ions within the WOC.
source: The results show that >30 mM NH2OH are needed in C12E8 dPSIIcc microcrystals to reduce all the Mn ions within the WOC (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), in contrast to PSII in solution, where 20 mM NH2OH are sufficient (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is based on EPR spectroscopy measurements on microcrystals.

claim: In PSII solution, 20 mM NH2OH are sufficient to reduce all the Mn ions within the WOC.
source: The results show that >30 mM NH2OH are needed in C12E8 dPSIIcc microcrystals to reduce all the Mn ions within the WOC (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), in contrast to PSII in solution, where 20 mM NH2OH are sufficient (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A and B).
evidence: This is based on EPR spectroscopy measurements on PSII solutions.

claim: The overall structures of apo-PSII and intact PSII are highly similar with Cα atoms superimposable to 4PJ0 with 0.209/0.225 Å rmsd (for the two PSII monomers).
source: The overall structures are highly similar and Cα atoms could be superimposed to 4PJ0 with 0.209/0.225 Å rmsd (for the two PSII monomers) and 0.218/0.191 Å (for the two D1 subunits), and to 3WU2 with 0.333/0.257 Å (monomers) and 0.246/0.242 Å (D1).
evidence: This is a quantitative structural comparison based on crystallographic data.

claim: Removal of the Mn4CaO5-cluster did not result in any discernible movement of subunits or domains.
source: Removal of the Mn4CaO5-cluster did not result in any discernible movement of subunits or domains, neither at the PSII donor side nor in the region of the membrane spanning helices or at the acceptor side, as illustrated by an overlay of the Cα atoms in D1 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a structural observation from comparison of apo-PSII and intact PSII structures.

claim: The extrinsic PsbU subunit in the monomer not involved in a crystal contact appeared destabilized.
source: However, the extrinsic PsbU subunit in the monomer not involved in a crystal contact appeared destabilized (Figure 3), in line with lability of PsbU binding to PSIIcc in solution in the presence of NH2OH/EDTA as discussed above.
evidence: This is based on B-factor analysis and electron density quality in the crystal structure.

claim: Crystal packing may have a direct effect on the WOC site.
source: From the B-factor analysis (Figure 3A) we suggest that accessibility and stability of the WOC of PSII treated with reducing and chelating agents may be influenced by a crystal contact involving PsbU. In the locked monomer the WOC is well protected by the intact PsbU subunit (see crystal contact discussed above in Figure 3A, inset, right) whereas in the unlocked monomer the WOC is easier accessible due to the more flexible, perturbed PsbU (no crystal contact in Figure 3A, inset, left). Thus, crystal packing may have a direct effect on the WOC site.
evidence: This is an inference from B-factor analysis and structural observations of the two monomers.

claim: The structure of PSII treated with 50 mM NH2OH/EDTA displays a clear lack of defined electron density at the site of the WOC.
source: The structure of PSII treated with 50 mM NH2OH/EDTA in the presence of 100 mM (NH4)2SO4, 100 mM Tris-HCl, pH 7.5, and 35% PEG 5000 MME, but in the absence of calcium, magnesium or manganese ions displays a clear lack of defined electron density at the site of the WOC (Figure 4B and C, Figure 4—figure supplement 1; see also Figure 4—figure supplements 2 and 3 for stereo views).
evidence: This is a direct observation from the electron density maps of the apo-PSII structure.

claim: Cluster-coordinating protein side chains are found in positions very similar to the native structure.
source: Cluster-coordinating protein side chains nevertheless are found in positions very similar to the native structure.
evidence: This is a structural observation from comparison of apo-PSII and intact PSII structures.

claim: Only Glu354, coordinating Mn2 and Mn3 and contributed by CP43, is no longer defined in the electron density and presumably assumes a number of alternative positions.
source: Only Glu354, coordinating Mn2 and Mn3 and contributed by CP43, is no longer defined in the electron density and presumably assumes a number of alternative positions.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the electron density maps of apo-PSII.

claim: The TyrZ-O-H—N-His190 H-bond clearly is maintained in the apo-PSII, at least at the proton activity present in the crystals (pH around 7.0–7.5).
source: In conclusion, the TyrZ-O-H—N-His190 H-bond clearly is maintained in the apo-PSII, at least at the proton activity present in the crystals (pH around 7.0–7.5).
evidence: This is a structural observation from the apo-PSII structure, though limited by resolution.

claim: Two peaks in the electron density map were observed in the absence of the WOC and have been tentatively assigned as water molecules.
source: In each monomer, two peaks in the electron density map were observed in the absence of the WOC and these have been tentatively assigned as water molecules.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the electron density maps of apo-PSII.

claim: The two water molecules are approximately located at the positions of the two oxygen atoms (O2 and O3) that bridge between Mn2 and Mn3 in the intact complex.
source: They are approximately located at the positions of the two oxygen atoms (O2 and O3) that bridge between Mn2 and Mn3 in the intact complex (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is a structural observation from comparison of apo-PSII and intact PSII structures.

claim: Two water molecules could be already sufficient to replace the 10 atoms of the Mn4CaO5 core of the assembled metal-cluster.
source: Inspection of a space-filling model of the emptied WOC site suggests that the gaps between Van-der-Waals spheres do not exceed 3 Å (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), suggesting that two water molecules could be already sufficient to replace the 10 atoms of the Mn4CaO5 core of the assembled metal-cluster.
evidence: This is an inference from structural modeling of the apo-WOC site.

claim: After removal of the Mn4CaO5-cluster, several formerly coordinating carboxylate side chains are at H-bonding distances to each other (≤3 Å).
source: Figure 5B shows that after removal of the Mn4CaO5-cluster, several formerly coordinating carboxylate side chains are at H-bonding distances to each other (≤3 Å; His332—Glu189—Asp342; (His337)—Asp342—OCO/Ala344), implying that one carboxylate of each H-bond pair is protonated.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the apo-PSII structure.

claim: The apo-PSII is characterized by pre-formed manganese binding sites, set up to facilitate correct assembly of the Mn4CaO5-cluster.
source: Consequently, the apo-PSII, which likely represents the starting state for metal-cluster (re-)assembly, is characterized by pre-formed manganese binding sites, set up to facilitate correct assembly of the Mn4CaO5-cluster.
evidence: This is an inference from the structural observation that coordinating residues maintain their positions.

claim: After manganese depletion of the dPSIIcc crystals, partial reassembly of the metal cluster was achieved.
source: After manganese depletion of the dPSIIcc crystals, we achieved partial reassembly of the metal cluster (see also Supplementary).
evidence: This is an experimental result from reconstitution experiments.

claim: The crystallographic data at 4.5 Å resolution for partially reconstituted PSII revealed electron density centered between the Mn1 and Mn2 binding site.
source: The corresponding crystallographic data at 4.5 Å resolution revealed electron density centered between the Mn1 and Mn2 binding site (Figure 6A and Figure 6—figure supplement 1A), compatible with manganese binding at these two sites.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the partially reconstituted PSII crystal structure.

claim: Partial disassembly experiments in the crystals showed electron density at 4.0 Å resolution centered around the Mn1 and Mn2 site.
source: We also conducted partial disassembly experiments (with lower NH2OH concentration) in the crystals and the obtained electron density at 4.0 Å resolution is centered around the Mn1 and Mn2 site (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), similar to the situation observed for the partial reassembly experiment.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the partially disassembled PSII crystal structure.

claim: A partially (dis)assembled state of the metal-cluster is formed where the Mn1 and Mn2 site are occupied and interconnected by two bridging oxides (Mn1-(µ-O)2-Mn2).
source: The joint evidence from these earlier investigations and our structural data render it plausible that a partially (dis)assembled state of the metal-cluster is formed where the Mn1 and Mn2 site are occupied and interconnected by two bridging oxides (Mn1-(µ-O)2-Mn2) in the same way as they are in the fully assembled Mn4CaO5-cluster.
evidence: This is an inference combining the current structural data with previous XAS studies.

claim: Investigations involving X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) support a di-µ-oxo bridged pair of Mn(III) ions as an intermediate in the heat-induced disassembly.
source: Investigations involving X-ray absorption spectroscopy (XAS) support a di-µ-oxo bridged pair of Mn(III) ions as an intermediate in the heat-induced disassembly (Pospísil et al., 2003), or as an intermediate state during photo-activation (Barra et al., 2006).
evidence: This is based on previous XAS studies cited in the text.

claim: Strong evidence based on pulsed EPR spectroscopy has been presented that a first step of the photo-activation process is the high-affinity binding of a Mn2+ ion occurring already in the dark at the Mn4 site.
source: Recently, strong evidence based on pulsed EPR spectroscopy has been presented that a first step of the photo-activation process is the high-affinity binding of a Mn2+ ion occurring already in the dark (before onset of illumination) by coordination to two specific axial ligands, Asp170 and Glu333, and thus at the Mn4 site (Asada and Mino, 2015), in line with earlier findings reviewed in (Bao and Burnap, 2016).
evidence: This is based on recent pulsed EPR spectroscopy studies.

claim: Only Mn4 is coordinated by two carboxylates in trans position.
source: Only Mn4 is coordinated by two carboxylates in trans position and we now find that this distinctive arrangement of Asp170 and Glu333 is maintained upon disassembly of the metal complex.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the apo-PSII structure.

claim: The distinctive arrangement of Asp170 and Glu333 is maintained upon disassembly of the metal complex.
source: Only Mn4 is coordinated by two carboxylates in trans position and we now find that this distinctive arrangement of Asp170 and Glu333 is maintained upon disassembly of the metal complex.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the apo-PSII structure.

claim: The structure of the metal-cluster site is largely identical when comparing fully functional PSII and apo-PSII, in remarkable contrast to many other metalloenzymes.
source: The structure of the metal-cluster site is largely identical when comparing fully functional PSII and apo-PSII, in remarkable contrast to many other metalloenzymes.
evidence: This is a comparative structural observation.

claim: A crystal structure in which the insertion of the catalytic [Mo-7Fe-9S-C] cluster of MoFe-containing nitrogenase was interrupted differs remarkably from the holo-protein.
source: For example, a crystal structure in which the insertion of the catalytic [Mo-7Fe-9S-C] cluster (Spatzal et al., 2011) of MoFe-containing nitrogenase was interrupted differs remarkably from the holo-protein and shows substantial conformational re-modeling in one of its three subunits whereby a positively charged funnel is created along which the cofactor may be inserted (Schmid et al., 2002).
evidence: This is based on previous structural studies of nitrogenase.

claim: The WOC is assembled in situ, in a multi-step process involving the oxidation of Mn ions at the metal binding site by the tyrosine radical (TyrZ●) formed under illumination.
source: In contrast to other complex metalloenzymes, whose metal-clusters are assembled on accessory scaffold proteins before being inserted into the target protein, the WOC is assembled in situ, in a multi-step process involving the oxidation of Mn ions at the metal binding site by the tyrosine radical (TyrZ●) formed under illumination (Cheniae and Martin, 1971; Dasgupta et al., 2008; Becker et al., 2011; Bao and Burnap, 2016).
evidence: This is established knowledge about WOC assembly, supported by citations.

claim: The almost perfectly pre-organized ligand shell likely facilitates kinetically competent and error-free formation of the metal complex upon light-driven oxidation of Mn ions.
source: This almost perfectly pre-organized ligand shell likely facilitates kinetically competent and error-free formation of the metal complex upon light-driven oxidation of Mn ions.
evidence: This is an inference from the structural observation of the pre-organized ligand shell.

claim: The apo-PSII structure serves as a basis to understand the mechanism of WOC assembly/disassembly in PSII.
source: We obtained the PSII structure for crystals completely depleted of the Mn4CaO5-cluster. This structure serves as a basis to understand the mechanism of WOC assembly/disassembly in PSII.
evidence: This is a statement about the significance of the structural data.

claim: The new apo-PSII structure showed a pre-organized ligand shell, including protein sidechains and water molecules assisting the stepwise auto-assembly of the active WOC.
source: Our new apo-PSII structure showed a pre-organized ligand shell, including protein sidechains and water molecules assisting the stepwise auto-assembly of the active WOC by offering a structuring template, directing metals and waters to places where they can be photo-activated/oxidized with minimal restructuring.
evidence: This is a structural observation and interpretation from the apo-PSII structure.

claim: The observations are in line with the XAS data in PSII solutions and compatible with the two-quantum model of photo-activation.
source: Our observations are thus in line with the XAS data in PSII solutions and compatible with the two-quantum model of photo-activation (Cheniae and Martin, 1971; Dasgupta et al., 2008; Becker et al., 2011; Bao and Burnap, 2016).
evidence: This is a statement comparing the current findings with previous studies and models.

claim: Data was collected on a single crystal of 100*80*60 µm3 that was previously treated with 50 mM NH2OH/EDTA and integrated to 2.55 Å resolution structure.
source: Data was collected on a single crystal of 100*80*60 µm3 that was previously treated with 50 mM NH2OH/EDTA and integrated to 2.55 Å resolution structure following the I/sigma(I) > 2 convention.
evidence: This is a description of the crystallographic data collection.

claim: 700 water molecules were placed in the apo-PSII structure, representing a quarter of those observed at higher resolution.
source: 700 water molecules were placed, representing a quarter of those observed at higher resolution in line with expectations (Weichenberger et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a description of the model building for the apo-PSII structure.

claim: In the apo-PSII structure, water molecules were not observed in place of the W1-4 oxo-ligands otherwise coordinating Mn4 and Ca.
source: They occupy similar positions compared to the high resolution structure (Figure 4B; overlays are shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and B); but in the apo-PSII structure we did not observe water molecules in place of the W1-4 oxo-ligands otherwise coordinating Mn4 and Ca.
evidence: This is a structural observation from the apo-PSII electron density maps.

claim: 96% of backbone torsion angles were in favored regions of the Ramachandran plot, 0.3% were outliers.
source: 96% of backbone torsion angles were in favored regions of the Ramachandran plot, 0.3% were outliers and the remaining residues were in additionally allowed regions.
evidence: This is a quality metric for the apo-PSII structure model.

claim: The final apo-PSII model was deposited in the protein data bank (PDB: 5MX2).
source: The final model was deposited in the protein data bank (PDB: 5MX2).
evidence: This is a statement about data deposition.

claim: The electron transfer from TyrZ to P680+ is coupled to movement of a proton to a neighboring histidine residue (D1-His190).
source: The electron transfer (ET) from a redox-active tyrosine residue (D1-Tyr161), denoted as TyrZ, to the chlorophyll cation radical, P680+, which was created by primary charge separation, is coupled to movement of a proton to a neighboring histidine residue (D1-His190).
evidence: This is established knowledge about proton-coupled electron transfer in PSII.

claim: This proton-coupled ET step has been found to be strongly slowed down upon Mn depletion and its rate becomes pH dependent.
source: This proton-coupled ET step has been found to be strongly slowed down upon Mn depletion and its rate becomes pH dependent (Styring et al., 2012).
evidence: This is based on previous studies of PSII function.

claim: A strong hydrogen bond of 2.4 Å length connects the redox active TyrZ and a histidine in D1 in PSII with assembled metal-cluster.
source: A strong hydrogen bond of 2.4 Å length (Umena et al., 2011) connects the redox active TyrZ and a histidine in D1 in PSII with assembled metal-cluster, whereas for the apo-PSII we determine a distance of 2.8 Å (and of 2.6 Å in the second, unlocked PSII monomer).
evidence: This is a structural comparison between intact PSII and apo-PSII.

claim: For the apo-PSII, the TyrZ-His190 distance is 2.8 Å in the locked monomer and 2.6 Å in the unlocked monomer.
source: A strong hydrogen bond of 2.4 Å length (Umena et al., 2011) connects the redox active TyrZ and a histidine in D1 in PSII with assembled metal-cluster, whereas for the apo-PSII we determine a distance of 2.8 Å (and of 2.6 Å in the second, unlocked PSII monomer).
evidence: This is a structural measurement from the apo-PSII structure.

claim: The absence of conformational changes in PSII may be due to crystal lattice forces.
source: As the WOC-free state was generated in the crystal, the absence of conformational changes in PSII may be due to crystal lattice forces, which can not only restrain the dissociation of subunits (PsbU, PsbV and PsbO) but also larger conformational changes near the WOC-binding site.
evidence: This is speculation about the reason for the lack of conformational changes.

claim: Local conformational changes in the cavity of the WOC are not restrained by the crystal packing as the residues are directed into a solvent filled cavity.
source: However, local conformational changes in the cavity of the WOC are not restrained by the crystal packing as the residues are directed into a solvent filled cavity.
evidence: This is an inference about the effect of crystal packing on the WOC site.

claim: Binuclear Fe or Mn sites found in other proteins share similar coordinating residues and bridging ligands with the WOC.
source: Interestingly, although the WOC is unique regarding structural complexity of the Mn4Ca metal site and light-driven Mn oxidation during assembly of the metal complex, binuclear Fe or Mn sites found in other proteins not only share similar coordinating residues and bridging ligands, but may also share a similar mode of oxidative self-assembly (Griese et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a comparison with other metalloenzymes based on literature.

claim: Binuclear Fe or Mn sites may share a similar mode of oxidative self-assembly with the WOC.
source: Interestingly, although the WOC is unique regarding structural complexity of the Mn4Ca metal site and light-driven Mn oxidation during assembly of the metal complex, binuclear Fe or Mn sites found in other proteins not only share similar coordinating residues and bridging ligands, but may also share a similar mode of oxidative self-assembly (Griese et al., 2014).
evidence: This is speculation based on comparison with other metalloenzymes.
